newsitem.title: CHINA: China Feb consumer price index up 5.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: China Feb consumer price index up 5.6 pct.

text.p: China's consumer price index rose 5.6 percent year-on-year in February, the State Statistical Bureau said on Tuesday.
The consumer price index was up a year-on-year 5.9 percent in January.
The bureau said that February's result continued a lengthy easing trend on the inflation front, though it said much of the rise in February prices was due to higher costs for food.
It also said that there was an upturn in new industrial and construction projects in the first two months of the year and that the government needed to step up its monitoring of the impact on costs.
There was no indication of an adjustment of the consumer price figures for the impact of the Chinese Lunar New Year holiday, which fell in February this year.
The bureau said the impact on consumer prices due to the holiday was most noticeable in food costs.
China's benchmark inflation indicator is the retail price index. In February, the retail price index climbed 2.9 percent after a 3.3 percent rise in January.
